My colleague overlooked a key fact: we do have Braxtatide's enzyme profile — it is a potent inducer of HTX-7M. Moradol is cleared almost entirely by HTX-1A. Since Braxtatide's induction target (HTX-7M) is a different enzyme from Moradol's clearance pathway (HTX-1A), enzyme-mediated acceleration of Moradol's metabolism is not expected. The remaining theoretical mechanisms — protein-binding displacement (Moradol is 92% bound) or altered absorption — have no supporting data for Braxtatide, but nothing suggests such an effect either. On the evidence available, no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction is indicated; the enzyme-based mechanism, the most plausible one, can be specifically excluded.

MECHANISM: Braxtatide induces HTX-7M; Moradol is cleared by HTX-1A — no shared enzyme, so no induction effect on Moradol clearance
